DAR CP5.1.0 (25March2026) sections1,4.3.1,5.5 protect off/unauthenticated states. Section5.5 explicitly limits SAN/NAS-drive protection to powered-off operation; running server/storage access remains a separate protection boundary.

Section7.4 permits unattended/datacenter use with managed dualDAR, secure-power response and anti-tamper/physical-control provisions. It does not convert ordinary always-mounted database storage into a complete approved DAR solution.

CP sections4.2,6,9 require a selected solution design and independent eligible layers. Two arbitrary AES implementations or FIPS certificates do not establish the full architecture; exact component configuration and registration remain relevant.

VID11574 SecurityTarget1.9 covers ONTAP9.16.1 NVE on enumerated NetApp FAS/AFF/ASA appliances. Volume encryption is transparent to block/file consumers. Section2.4 excludes cloud environments,VMware,protocol-security evaluation,HA,KMIP,SnapLock; evaluated management is serialCLI rather than SSH. Listed software cannot be transplanted to arbitrary cloud hardware.

Evaluated hardware is specific Dell Latitude/Precision models (e.g.Latitude5430/i7-1265U,Precision3260/i7-12700). Searched current published Components List for Istio, Envoy, ztunnel, Chainguard, Node.js, NGINX and PostgreSQL: no matching entry. Relevant categories inspected: TLS software applications/protected servers, IPsec gateways and MACsec. Product listing is distinct from FIPS validation; evaluated identity/version and CP configuration matter.

MSC1.3 §4.1.1 places the Red network behind the inner encryption component; it permits unencrypted classified traffic there. §§4/4.2 protect same-security-level sites across untrusted transport using two independent nested IPsec/MACsec tunnels. This is a network-boundary architecture, not a mandate to insert two CSfC layers between every pair of pods within one authorized Red enclave.

MSC1.3 tables6/7 distinguish current CNSA1 threshold suites from CNSA2 objectives: AES256, P384/RSA3072 and SHA384/512 are not equivalent to an unrestricted FIPS algorithm set. Product, protocol and topology requirements still apply; selecting a cipher is not a complete CSfC solution.

MA2.8 §5.6 permits a specifically selected TLS-protected server as the inner encryption component for a TLS end-user-device design; §§12.2 tables16/17 define TLS algorithm requirements. This differs from the MSC IPsec/MACsec site-to-site architecture and does not make arbitrary application TLS an approved inner component.

MA2.8 table16 specifies CNSA1 TLS encryption AES256-GCM, authentication RSA3072 or ECDSA P384/SHA384, and key establishment ECDH P384 or DH3072; table17 adds CNSA2 algorithms as applicable. TLS1.3 by itself does not constrain all these selections.

Actual candidate Core1.14 gateway template sets minimumTLS1.3(default), optionalTLS1.2, and referenced server certificate Secrets; it does not set an explicit CNSA-only cipher/curve/key-assurance profile.

Root PeerAuthentication selects STRICT workload mTLS. This is product transport protection within the enrolled mesh; no CSfC registration or listed network-component identity is established by this setting.
Core1.14 unicorn values select ztunnel-fips:v1.30.3. Core package version1.14 is not Istio/ztunnel version1.14; its mesh software baseline is1.30.3.
Core1.14 unicorn values select Istio pilot/proxy FIPS1.30.3. A vendor-supported FIPS variant is useful evidence for ordinary FIPS controls but is not a current NSA-listed product match.

Upstream matching1.30.3 provider code permits TLS13_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS13_AES_128_GCM_SHA256. The tls-boring FIPS-only branch comment explicitly lists both; tls-openssl/aws-lc/ring branches also include both. This establishes that the ordinary baseline is not an AES256-only CNSA profile, without claiming a particular connection negotiated AES128 or that vendor image patches were independently reproduced.

Upstream matching1.30.3 CSR branches generate P256 keys (PRIME256V1 or PKCS_ECDSA_P256_SHA256). No Core source override to a P384-only CNSA certificate profile was found. Vendor build identity still needs to be matched before asserting its exact negotiated runtime profile.
